overview: Madagascar is a large island country in the Indian Ocean, off the south-east coast of Africa, and the fourth-largest island in the world. Its capital and largest city is Antananarivo. Its first settlers came from South-East Asia, and the Malagasy language is related to languages spoken in Indonesia. Madagascar became independent from France in 1960.

geography.text: A high central plateau runs down the length of Madagascar, with rainforest on the wetter east side and drier forests, grassland and spiny desert in the west and south. Because the island has been separated from other land for millions of years, most of its animals and plants, including lemurs, are found nowhere else on Earth.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical on the coasts, cooler in the highlands.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Lemurs, chameleons and baobab trees found nowhere else.

history.text: Madagascar was settled by people from South-East Asia and East Africa between about 1,500 and 2,000 years ago. The Merina kingdom unified much of the island in the 1800s. France conquered Madagascar in 1895 and brutally put down an uprising in 1947. It became independent in 1960.

events.title: Radama I
events.text: The Merina king begins unifying the island.

events.title: Malagasy Uprising
events.text: A revolt against French rule is crushed.

government.text: Madagascar has had several coups and political crises. In October 2025 youth-led protests over water and power cuts were followed by a military takeover, and President Andry Rajoelina fled the country.

economy.text: Madagascar is the world's largest producer of vanilla. It also exports cloves, nickel, cobalt and textiles. Most people are farmers growing rice, and it is one of the poorest countries in the world.

culture.text: Madagascar split from other landmasses so long ago that about 90% of its plants and animals are found nowhere else, including all of the world's lemurs. The Avenue of the Baobabs is lined with giant ancient trees. Famadihana, 'the turning of the bones', is a ceremony honouring ancestors.

items.title: Lemurs
items.text: More than 100 species, found only in Madagascar.

items.title: Avenue of the Baobabs
items.text: Giant trees up to 800 years old.

items.title: Vanilla
items.text: Most of the world's vanilla comes from here.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Romazava, a meat and greens stew, with rice.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Famadihana, the turning of the bones, honours ancestors.

sport.text: Rugby union is the national sport and draws huge crowds in Antananarivo. In football, Madagascar reached the Africa Cup of Nations quarter-finals at its first attempt in 2019.
